issues.legal_issue: A statutory tribunal constituted of a president and two assessors must adjudicate compensation and land-measurement disputes as a three-member body, rather than through the president alone.
material_facts: The governing statute constituted the tribunal of a president and two assessors.
In the cases before the Court, the assessors did not participate in hearing the arguments, and the president made the awards alone.
The president recorded that the assessors had told him to hear the arguments by himself and were not present.
issues.conclusion: The three members’ presence and participation in the adjudication were mandatory. Awards made by the president alone were not awards of the tribunal and were void; the High Court judgments and the awards under appeal were set aside, with the disputes to be decided by a properly constituted tribunal.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 58 and 60 of the Punjab Improvement Trust Act, 1922 provide for a tribunal consisting of a president and two assessors. Sections 59 and 65 treat the tribunal’s award as a court award and provide for its enforcement; section 59 gives the president specified powers concerning evidence and questions of law, title and procedure, but does not make him the sole adjudicator of compensation or measurement disputes. Section 26 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 treats an award as a decree and judgment. Read together, these provisions require adjudication by the tribunal as a composite three-member body, with a majority decision where members disagree. The Court rejected the contrary reasoning in Sohan Lal v. State of Haryana, AIR 1981 Punjab and Haryana 349.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_reference and tribunal_has_three_statutory_members and president_decided_alone and assessors_did_not_participate_in_adjudication

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_reference: The proceeding concerns a reference for determination of compensation for acquired land.
predicates.tribunal_has_three_statutory_members: The law constituting the tribunal provides for a president and two assessors as its members.
predicates.president_decided_alone: The president made the decision on compensation or land measurement without the other members deciding it with him.
predicates.assessors_did_not_participate_in_adjudic: The assessors did not participate in the adjudication of the compensation or land-measurement dispute.

issues.definition: When a compensation reference is assigned by law to a three-member tribunal and the president decides it alone without the assessors participating, the president’s award is void.

issues.legal_issue: The doctrine of stare decisis does not require adherence to an earlier interpretation that is plainly erroneous on the statutory jurisdiction or composition of a tribunal and defeats the statute’s purpose.
material_facts: A High Court decision had held that the tribunal’s president could make an award alone, and that interpretation had been followed for a period before its legality was challenged.
The earlier interpretation concerned who had jurisdiction to make the statutory tribunal’s award and, in the Supreme Court’s view, contradicted the statute’s requirement for a three-member tribunal.
The Court considered that adhering to the earlier interpretation would perpetuate an invalid adjudication and defeat the statutory purpose.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to follow the earlier High Court interpretation and held that stare decisis did not preserve it.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the principles discussed in The Keshav Mills Co. Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bombay North, AIR 1965 SC 1636, including the need for compelling reasons and substantial agreement before overruling a Supreme Court decision, and on Maktul v. Mst. Manbhari, AIR 1985 SC 918; Bengal Immunity Co. Ltd. v. State of Bihar, [1955] 2 SCR 603; A.R. Antulay v. R.S. Nayak, [1988] 2 SCC 602; Raj Narain Pandey v. Sant Prasad Tiwari, [1973] 2 SCC 35; Darshan Singh v. Rampal Singh, [1992] Supp. 1 SCC 191; and Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala, AIR 1973 SC 1461. A precedent followed over time is ordinarily respected, but the doctrine is not inflexible where the earlier interpretation is plainly erroneous, concerns jurisdiction or statutory interpretation, or would perpetuate serious legal error. The Court distinguished decisions applying stare decisis to settled rights or rules not involving such a statutory jurisdictional error.

predicates.challenge_to_statutory_tribunal_jurisdic: A proceeding challenges whether the statutory tribunal had jurisdiction to decide the dispute in the manner it did.
predicates.earlier_interpretation_permits_adjudicat: An earlier judicial interpretation allowed fewer members to decide a matter than the statute provides for the tribunal.
predicates.earlier_interpretation_is_plainly_errone: The court concludes that the earlier interpretation contradicts the statute and would defeat its purpose.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns a tribunal’s statutory jurisdiction, and an earlier plainly erroneous interpretation allowed fewer than the required members to adjudicate, stare decisis does not require that interpretation to be followed.

issues.legal_issue: Acquiescence by a party cannot confer jurisdiction on a tribunal or validate an award made contrary to a mandatory statutory composition requirement.
material_facts: It was argued that the appellant had acquiesced in awards made by a single member of the tribunal.
The Court held that the awards had been made by the president alone despite the statutory requirement for adjudication by the tribunal as a three-member body.
issues.conclusion: Acquiescence did not confer jurisdiction or validate the single-member awards.
issues.legal_principle: A party’s acquiescence cannot cure the failure to satisfy a mandatory statutory requirement that determines the composition and jurisdiction of a quasi-judicial tribunal. The Court applied its construction of sections 58, 59 and 60 of the Punjab Improvement Trust Act, 1922, under which adjudication by the three-member tribunal was imperative.

predicates.challenge_to_statutory_tribunal_jurisdic: A proceeding challenges whether a statutory tribunal had authority to make the award in the manner it did.
predicates.mandatory_member_requirement_not_met: The tribunal did not satisfy a statutory requirement governing which members must participate in adjudication.
predicates.party_acquiesced_to_adjudication: A party accepted, participated in, or did not object to the adjudication by the improperly constituted decision-maker.

issues.definition: If a party acquiesced in an adjudication that failed a mandatory statutory member requirement, that acquiescence does not validate the award when the tribunal’s jurisdiction is challenged.

issues.legal_issue: The ruling that a single-member award is invalid applies to awards under challenge, but does not unsettle single-member awards that had already become final.
material_facts: The awards at issue were challenged in pending proceedings and the Court set aside the awards under appeal.
The Court was asked to apply its ruling only prospectively so that the awards under appeal would remain undisturbed.
The Court stated that single-member awards already made and having become final would not be unsettled.
issues.conclusion: The Court refused to preserve the awards under appeal by applying its ruling only prospectively, while expressly leaving undisturbed single-member awards that had already become final.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered Managing Director, ECIL, Hyderabad v. B. Karunakar, [1993] 4 SCC 727, where a newly stated principle was given prospective operation, but held that the circumstances here did not justify preserving awards under appeal. It declared that single-member awards made from the date of judgment would be void and that awards already made and final would not be reopened.

predicates.challenge_to_single_member_tribunal_awar: A proceeding challenges an award made by the president of a statutory tribunal without the other required members participating.
predicates.award_is_under_review_before_becoming_fi: The challenged award remains under judicial review and has not become final.

issues.definition: A challenged single-member award that remains under review is not preserved as a final award, while single-member awards that had already become final remain undisturbed.
